answer.answer: No—not by itself. A recorded supervision event or completed reconciliation can evidence an activity, but does not establish its adequacy or the propriety of ownership records. That conclusion requires an applicable legal standard and reliable facts showing that the activity met that standard for the relevant actor, product, risks and period. The retained provisions supply qualitative requirements and relevant considerations, not a rule equating completion with fulfillment.

claims.proposition: Retained responsibility and fulfilled responsibility are distinct conclusions.

support.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.
the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds.

claims.inference: Text: responsibility survives outsourcing. Deduction: recording an oversight activity does not itself establish fulfillment of that responsibility.
missing_premises: The retained edition applies to the product, activity and assessment period, including applicable conditions or modifications.
The entity is the relevant Product Provider.
An applicable standard for discharging responsibility and facts demonstrating compliance with it.

claims.proposition: A recorded supervision event does not alone establish adequate supervision.
claims.status: Source-supported deduction; adequacy assessment requires facts

support.quote: Where a third party is engaged in the valuation of a scheme, the management company shall exercise reasonable care, skill and diligence in the selection, appointment and ongoing monitoring of such third party in ensuring such entity possesses the appropriate level of knowledge, experience and resources that commensurate with the appropriate valuation policies and procedures for each scheme.
The valuation activities of such third party should be subject to ongoing supervision and periodic review by the management company.
This UT Code does not have the force of law.

claims.inference: Text: UT 6.11C supplies a valuation-specific care standard and ongoing supervision requirement. Deduction: an event log alone does not establish the quality, continuity or effectiveness of supervision. Applying that standard to other tokenisation activities would require a separate legal warrant.
missing_premises: Applicability of UT 6.11C: the entity is the management company and the third party performs scheme valuation.
Any applicable authorization conditions, modifications or relaxations.
Reliable evidence of supervision over the relevant period, including its scope, frequency, reviewer competence, findings and responses.
Evidence that selection, appointment and monitoring addressed the third party's knowledge, experience and resources.

claims.proposition: A completed reconciliation is relevant evidence but does not alone establish proper ownership records.

support.quote: Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

whether the ownership interest of the underlying assets of the Tokenised Securities are legally valid under the applicable governing laws, whether there are regular reconciliations between the records for the extrinsic rights and the records for the distributed ledger tokens, or whether any encumbrance affects the extrinsic rights.
For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

claims.inference: Text: paragraph 11 requires proper ownership-interest records; the Appendix identifies regular reconciliation alongside legal validity and encumbrances. Deduction: completion of a reconciliation establishes neither that the compared records are correct nor that they reflect legally valid ownership. The evidence listed below is a proposed assessment approach, not an exhaustive checklist prescribed by the text.
missing_premises: A justified standard for what constitutes proper records in this product's legal and operational arrangements.
The governing ownership rights, settlement-finality rules and status of on-chain and off-chain records.
Reliable evidence of reconciliation coverage, frequency, source-data accuracy, discrepancies and their resolution throughout the relevant period.
Evidence that records identify the relevant holders and their actual interests, including relevant encumbrances.
Evidence of operational compatibility with involved service providers.

rival_readings: An allocation-focused reading of paragraph 10 emphasizes that ultimate responsibility remains with the Product Provider; it does not establish that particular supervisory conduct or records fulfill the substantive requirements.

Conduct-focused, outcome-focused and combined assessments may demand different evidence of fulfillment. The quoted provisions do not establish an exhaustive discharge test or make a single event, reconciliation, or favorable outcome conclusive.
unresolved: No actual supervision or reconciliation evidence is supplied for assessment.
The applicable adequacy threshold, assessment period and product-specific authorization conditions remain unestablished.
UT 6.11C is valuation-specific; its standard cannot automatically be transferred to every Product Provider or outsourced activity.
The provisions retain their distinct wording and regulatory context: SHOULD, shall and must are not interchangeable proof of statutory duties.
The supplied parser, graph and serialization results cannot supply missing legal standards, factual evidence or proof of fulfillment.
